Netherlands – Electrical installation work – Framework Agreement Battery Energy Storage Systems - Energielandschap Lageland
description: The Client intends to enter into a framework agreement (the Agreement) with three contractors for the realisation of the Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) at Energielandschap Lageland. The specific contracts under the Agreement will be put out to tender as turnkey EPC contracts for the Energielandschap Lageland battery park. The Client is procuring a functional end product: a ready-to-use, grid-compliant and safe battery system that meets the performance requirements set out in the tender specifications. The EPC contractor is responsible for the design, supply, construction, system integration, testing, commissioning and handover of a ready-to-use battery system, as well as (via a separate O&M agreement) for its long-term operation and maintenance. - Phase 1: approximately 15 MW // 60 MWh BESS, connected to a 21 MW grid connection, with commissioning planned for Q1 2029. - Phase 2: expansion to at least 50 MW // 200 MWh BESS, in conjunction with the upscaling of the connection (feed-in up to 260 MW, off-take up to 145 MW). Phase 2 is not being awarded at this stage, but is secured within the framework agreement and will be called off later via a mini-competition between the framework contractors. The indicative timetable is around 2032/2033, subject to TenneT’s approval.

title: Z1DA--B170 Window Recaulking Services
description: SF 30 CONTINUATION SHEET AMENDMENT 0002 Solicitation No.: 36C25627Q0022 Project: B170 Courtyard Window Re Caulk CAVHS Purpose of Amendment The purpose of this amendment is to provide the Government s responses to vendor questions submitted prior to the deadline. The following Questions & Answers are hereby incorporated into the solicitation. These clarifications do not change the scope of work unless explicitly stated. Only the Contracting Officer may authorize changes per FAR 52.212 4(c). SECTION: QUESTIONS & ANSWERS General Administrative Items Q1. Will the Government confirm that offers should be submitted via email to andrew.misfeldt@va.gov? A1. Yes. Submit one consolidated PDF ( 10MB), font Arial 11, in accordance with the solicitation instructions. Q2. Are there page limitations? A2. No page limits apply. The file-size limit of 10MB governs. Q3. Which form must be submitted SF 1449 or SF 1442? A3. Offerors shall submit a signed SF 1449. SF 1442 is not required. Evaluation Factors Q4. Please confirm the evaluation factors. A4. Evaluation consists of: Factor I Approach & Quality Management Factor II Professional Qualifications & Specialized Experience Factor III Past Performance Factor IV Price Factors I III are equal in importance and collectively approximately equal to Price. Q5. Does managing one subcontractor satisfy Past Performance requirements? A5. Yes, provided the offeror served as the prime contractor. Site Visit, Access, & Logistics Q6. Will there be a site visit? A6. A site visit was held on October 14, 2026. No additional site visits will be conducted. Q7. Please confirm logistical restrictions. A7. Approximate curtainwall height is 50 ft (verify independently). Elevator weight limit is 4,000 lbs. Courtyard door widths are 36 58 . Quiet hours are 2 3 PM and 10 PM 5 AM. Coordinate courtyard occupation with nursing staff. Q8. Are badges required? A8. Not for courtyard work during business hours. Badges are required for roof access. Delays caused by incomplete contractor submissions are not excusable delays. Scope Clarifications Q9. Does work occur along the entire curtainwall or only at leak locations? A9. Work shall occur along the entire curtainwall interface within Courtyards 1B and 1C to provide a continuous and complete seal. Q10. Should the entire length be repaired for a uniform seal? A10. Yes. Q11. Are cover caps replaced everywhere? A11. No. Replace only caps that are missing or cannot be reattached. Q12. Are other courtyard walls included? A12. No. Only the curtainwall/TPO/wall interface is included unless otherwise directed by the CO. Q13. Will the Government provide as builts or record drawings? A13. No. They are not available. Q14. Will the Government provide quantities? A14. No. Offerors must determine all quantities during the site visit. These measurements are binding for proposal purposes. Q15. Is full perimeter window caulking included? A15. No. Only the interfaces described in the SOW apply. Q16. Clarify termination bar installation. A16. Install the bar above the cant strip to secure the existing TPO using fasteners compatible with the substrate. Q17. Clarify face cap/flashing quantities. A17. Approximately 14 vertical caps have slid; one horizontal cap is missing; two require replacement. Remove flashing attached to the ground level base face cap. Offerors must verify all quantities. Q18. Will the awning require removal? A18. Not anticipated. Do not include awning removal unless CO directed. Q19. How many pavers must be moved and how should they be stored? A19. Approximately 70 pavers must be moved. Store in the courtyard, stacking no more than six high. Specifications, Submittals, & Warranty Q20. Which parts of VA 07 54 23 apply? A20. Membrane accessory materials and compatibility requirements apply. VA 07 92 00 applies to sealant products. Where requirements conflict, the more stringent governs. Q21. Confirm applicability of installer approvals, warranty, submittals, and pre installation meeting. A21. Manufacturer-approved roofing installer: Not required. Sealant warranty: 10-year manufacturer warranty required. Submittals: Required for sealants and termination materials showing compatibility. Pre installation meeting: Required prior to NTP; the 30 day PoP begins after NTP issuance. Q22. Provide TPO manufacturer or warranty info. A22. Unknown. Contractor is not responsible for maintaining prior warranties and shall ensure compatibility of materials. Schedule & Period of Performance Q23. Will NTP be flexible due to temperature/weather? A23. Yes. NTP may be adjusted as appropriate. Excusable delays are handled per FAR 52.212 4(f). Q24. Are background checks/PIV issuance included in the PoP? A24. Yes. Badges only required for roof access. Delays arising from incomplete contractor submissions are not excusable. Q25. Will water spray or infiltration testing be required? A25. No. Optional testing may be performed at the contractor s cost unless CO directed. Q26. Anticipated award/NTP date? A26. Award is anticipated on or around November 1, 2026 (subject to change). Schedule adjustments for weather may be considered if CO approved. Labor Standards, Set Aside, Subcontracting, & Bonds Q27. Which wage determination applies? A27. Davis Bacon Wage Determination AR20260032 applies. Q28. Will the contract be issued under DBRA only? A28. Yes. Any SCLS references are not applicable and will be conformed administratively. Q29. Which limitations on subcontracting apply? A29. Construction limitations apply. For special trade construction, no more than 75% (excluding materials) may be subcontracted to non similarly situated entities. LOS certification must be submitted. Q30. Are performance and payment bonds required? A30. No. Bonds are not required under this solicitation unless added by future amendment. Q31. Confirm SDVOSB status requirements. A31. This is a total SDVOSB set aside. Offerors must be certified in the SBA database at time of offer and award. Materials & Trades Q32. Will brake metal caps be accepted if originals are unavailable? A32. Yes, if they closely match existing caps and are approved before installation. Q33. Is a glazing contractor required? A33. No. Quantities & Pricing Basis Q34. Can VA provide LF quantities of termination bar or number of caps? A34. No. Offerors must determine quantities during the site visit. Q35. Should offerors price awning removal? A35. No. Do not include awning removal unless CO directed. Unforeseen/Differing Site Conditions Q36. How will additional TPO damage discovered during work be handled? A36. Repairs beyond the defined scope may only be performed if directed in writing by the Contracting Officer. Entitlement will be determined at that time. Q37. Are leaks associated with recent renovations? A37. No. Leaks have been occurring since the membrane was installed. Attachments Q38. Are photos/figures available? A38. Yes. title: FCI Sheridan Water Loop Repair
description: FCI SHERIDAN WATER LOOP REPAIR Solicitation No. 15B61227Q00000001 Project No. 26Z6AV4 The Federal Bureau of Prisons, FCI Sheridan, requests firm-fixed-price quotations for repairs to the underground pre-insulated hot-water distribution loop at 27072 SW Ballston Road, Sheridan, Oregon 97378. This acquisition is a total small business set-aside. The contractor shall provide all labor, supervision, technical engineering, equipment, materials, and incidentals necessary to complete repairs at Locations A and B, including structural pipe lining, mechanical repairs, excavation, testing, and surface restoration. The SF 1449, amendments, and attached Statement of Work and Drawings establish the solicitation requirements. The Statement of Work and Drawings are incorporated into this solicitation and the resulting award. QUOTATION SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS Submit the following: 1. Price Provide a firm-fixed-price quotation for CLIN 0001 covering the complete requirement, including security coordination, testing, restoration, warranties, and temporary hot-water contingency measures required by the SOW. Identify any assumptions or exceptions. 2. Technical Approach Submit a technical narrative not exceeding five pages addressing: � The repair approach and sequence for Locations A and B. � The proposed structural liner�s suitability for the specified temperatures and pressures, installation and curing procedures, and manufacturer warranty. � Excavation, welding, insulation restoration, leak-detection continuity, hydrostatic testing, and surface restoration. � The proposed completion schedule, including mobilization, personnel clearances, material availability, shutdowns, and testing. � How the work will satisfy the eight-consecutive-hour hot-water outage restriction per housing unit, including the temporary boiler contingency required by the SOW. � Coordination of escorts, tool control, utility isolation, and institutional work restrictions. Manufacturer technical data and warranty documentation are excluded from the five-page limit. Alternative products or components must include the technical documentation, certifications, and test results required by the SOW. 3. Relevant Experience Describe up to three comparable projects involving underground hot-water piping repairs or high-temperature structural pipe lining. Identify the scope, completion date, customer contact information, and whether the quoter performed as prime contractor or subcontractor. These descriptions are excluded from the technical approach page limit. ORAL PRESENTATIONS Each quoter submitting a timely quotation will participate in a virtual oral presentation of up to 30 minutes, including Government questions. The Government will provide scheduling instructions after quotation receipt. The proposed project manager or technical lead shall explain the repair approach, schedule, outage management, temporary hot-water contingency, and principal performance risks. Prepared slides are not required. The Government will evaluate information provided during the presentation together with the written quotation. Oral statements do not change solicitation requirements. Commitments relied upon for award shall be documented in writing and incorporated into the resulting contract. EVALUATION The Government will evaluate: 1. Technical approach. 2. Relevant experience and past performance. 3. Price. Technical approach and relevant experience and past performance, when combined, are more important than price. Technical approach will be evaluated for understanding of the requirement, feasibility of the repair sequence, suitability of proposed materials, and ability to meet technical, testing, security, restoration, schedule, and outage requirements. Relevant experience and past performance will be evaluated for similarity to the required work and demonstrated quality of performance. The Government may consider customer references, CPARS, and other available information, including performance as a subcontractor. A lack of relevant past performance information will receive a neutral assessment and will not be evaluated favorably or unfavorably. Price will be evaluated for completeness and fairness and reasonableness. CONFIDENCE RATINGS The Government will assign separate confidence ratings for technical approach and relevant experience and past performance, supported by documented findings: High Confidence: The Government has high confidence that the quoter understands the requirement, proposes a sound approach, and will successfully perform with little or no Government intervention. Some Confidence: The Government has some confidence in successful performance, but identified concerns may require Government intervention. Low Confidence: The Government has low confidence in successful performance, even with Government intervention. A neutral past performance assessment will not, by itself, increase or decrease confidence. STREAMLINED EVALUATION PROCESS The evaluation team will use on-the-spot consensus following review of each written quotation and oral presentation. The Government will document the findings supporting its conclusions. When multiple quotations are received, the Government may use comparative evaluation to assess their relative benefits and risks under the stated factors. The award decision will consider the underlying findings rather than ratings alone. BASIS FOR AWARD Award will be made to the responsible quoter whose quotation meets the solicitation requirements and provides the best value to the Government. The Government may select a higher-priced quotation when its evaluated benefits justify the additional price. If only one quotation is received, the Government will evaluate it against the stated requirements and factors and determine whether its price is fair and reasonable before award. The Government may communicate with quoters and request revised quotations as necessary. Quoters should submit their best initial quotation because award may be made without requesting revisions. SUBMISSION DEADLINE AND CONTACT Quotations are due October 29, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. Pacific Time, unless changed by a subsequent amendment. Submit quotations electronically to d1palmer@bop.gov. Identify solicitation number 15B61227Q00000001 in the subject line and acknowledge all solicitation amendments.

description: BIDS RECEIVED BY FAX AND EMAIL WILL BE ACCEPTED AS OFFICIAL. PARKS CANADA IS NOT CURRENTLY ACCEPTING BIDS VIA SAP ARIBA, YOU MUST SUBMIT YOUR BID VIA FAX OR EMAIL AS INDICATED IN THE SOLICITATION DOCUMENT. BIDS RECEIVED IN-PERSON OR BY COURIER WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED. The only acceptable email address for responses to the bid solicitation is soumissionsami-bidsrpc@pc.gc.ca. Bids submitted by email directly to the Contracting Authority or to any email address other than soumissionsami-bidsrpc@pc.gc.ca will not be accepted. The only acceptable facsimile for responses to bid solicitations is 1-855-983-1808. The maximum email file size that Parks Canada is capable of receiving is 15 megabytes. The Bidder is responsible for any failure attributable to the transmission or receipt of the emailed bid due to file size. The Bidder should be cognisant of the size of the email as a whole, and not only the attachments. Please take into consideration that some attachments, when sent, may be resized during the email transfer. If the email size is too large, the Bidder should send the bid in multiple emails properly labeled with the solicitation number, project name, and indicate how many emails are included (ex. 1 of 2). Emails with links to bid documents will not be accepted. Bid documents must be sent as email attachments. REQUIREMENT Parks Canada Agency (PCA) requires the services of a Contractor for repair and improvements to the floats, connections mooring and interior systems of the Gwaii Haanas Float Camp. TWO-SUBMISSION BID This Bid shall be submitted following a “two-submission” procedure. Refer to SI03 of the Special Instructions to Bidders. CONTRACTOR SELECTION AND INDIGENOUS PARTICIPATION PLAN The Contractor should ensure provision of specific and agreed upon benefits for Indigenous People and Indigenous Businesses in the Area of the Contract. This Invitation to Tender contains bid criteria in order to provide socioeconomic benefits to Indigenous communities within the area covered by the contract. PERIOD OF CONTRACT / DELIVERY DATE Contractor must perform and complete the Work no later than October 31, 2027. ENQUIRIES All enquiries of a technical and contractual nature are to be submitted to the Contracting Authority. Enquiries regarding this solicitation must be submitted in writing and should be received no later than five (5) business days prior to the date set for solicitation closing to allow sufficient time to provide a response. Enquiries received after that time may result in an answer NOT being provided. INFORMATION National Parks Regulations require that all work is to be performed in accordance with the ordinances, laws, rules and regulations set out in the National Park Act. Bidders that consider themselves qualified to provide this Work and intend to submit bids on this project should obtain documents from the Government Electronic Tendering Service through the Government of Canada tendering service at http://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities. Addenda, when issued, will be available from the Government of Canada tendering service. Bidders that elect to base their bids on documents obtained from other sources do so at their own risk. Late submissions will not be considered. The Crown retains the right to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. Parks Canada has made every effort to provide equivalent documents in both official languages, however, if you find any discrepancies between the English and French documents, please notify the contract officer listed in this opportunity as soon as possible so that we can rectify the situation.

title: Germany – Architectural, engineering and planning services – Generalplanungsleistungen für die denkmalgerechte Teilsanierung des GAT-Bereichs im ehemaligen Flughafen Tempelhof
description: Das eingeschossige GAT-Gebäude, ein zwischen 1951 und 1953 als Abfertigungsgebäude für den zivilen Flugverkehr errichteter Anbau des Flughafens Tempelhof, befindet sich im westlichen Flügel des Flughafens zwischen den Treppentürmen 5 und 6. Es liegt zwischen der Landseite des Flughafens und den Flugsteigen auf dem überdachten Vorfeld, dem sogenannten Transit-Gang im Bauteil A1. Der Planungsbereich (BGF: 959 qm) umfasst das Bauvolumen der eingeschossigen GAT-Erweiterung zwischen den Treppentürmen 5 und 6 sowie zwischen den Außenräumen vor dem Eingang und der Bauteiltrennwand zum Transitgang im Gebäude A1. . Der Planungsauftrag erfolgt stufenweise und umfasst die Leistungsphasen 1 bis 8 für die Grundleistungen aller relevanten Planungen der beschriebenen Leistungen gem. HOAI zu 100%. Dabei gilt: - Leistungsstufe 1: LP 1-2 - Leistungsstufe 2: LP 3-4 - Leistungsstufe 3: LP 5-7 - Leistungsstufe 4: LP 8 Ein Anspruch des Auftragnehmers auf Abruf der Leistungsstufe 2-4 besteht nicht.

title: Chemical Nutrient Analysis Service for Combat Feeding Division (CFD)
description: The U.S. Army Contracting Command � Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG), Natick Division, in support of the U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command � Soldier Center (DEVCOM-SC), Soldier Sustainment Directorate (SSD) / Combat Feeding Division (CFD) located in Natick, MA 01760, has a requirement for chemical nutrient analysis services for the U.S. Army Combat Feeding Division. The Combat Feeding Division�s Nutrient Analysis Laboratory (NAL) currently has multiple samples to analyze for nutritional content. The CFD, part of the U.S. Army DEVCOM-SC, is the Department of Defense�s centralized source for all research, development, engineering, and integration of joint service combat rations, food service equipment and field feeding systems. title: NEXODOSE DOSE MONITOR
description: This is a SOURCES SOUGHT announcement only. It is neither a solicitation announcement nor a request for proposal or quote and does not obligate the Government to award a contract. Responses to this Sources Sought must be in writing. The purpose of this Sources Sought Announcement is for market research, to make appropriate acquisition decisions, and to gain knowledge of potential qualified businesses capable of providing the following: DoseMonitor/Nexodose Management for Kansas and Missouri VA Medical Facilities *** See Statement of Work below for details *** If this is within your capability, please respond with the information below: Company Name Address Point of Contact Phone, Fax, and Email UEI number GSA Contract (as applicable) Capability Statement that clearly and convincingly identifies your ability to fulfill this requirement. Brochures of product being offered to include specifications. Authorized service provider letter from OEM Interested firms are reminded that in accordance with FAR 4.203, prospective contractors shall complete electronic annual representations and certifications to be considered for award. In addition, FAR 4.203 states that prospective contractors shall be registered in the System for Award Management (www.SAM.gov) database. All Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB) and Veteran Owned Small Businesses (VOSB) shall be verified in SBA at Small Business Search . Point of Contact for this Sources Sought is: veronica.flores@va.gov Department of Veterans Affairs Network Contracting Office -15 3450 S. 4th Street Trafficway Leavenworth, KS. 66048 STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) Radiation Dose Tracking Software Maintenance, Support, and Bi-Directional HL7 Interface Services (DoseMonitor/Nexodose) Department of Veterans Affairs Veterans Integrated Service Network (Legacy VISN) Kansas and Missouri VA Medical Facilities: Period of Performance (Base Year): 02/01/2027 � 01/31/2028 Period of Performance (Option Year 1): 02/01/2028 � 01/31/2029 1. BACKGROUND Kansas and Missouri VA Medical Facilities currently utilizes the DoseMonitor (Nexodose) radiation dose tracking and monitoring software platform to capture, track, and report patient radiation exposure associated with diagnostic and interventional imaging procedures. This system supports clinical safety, regulatory compliance (e.g., accreditation and federal radiation safety reporting), and quality assurance functions for Radiology and related imaging services at the facility identified above. The facility's DoseMonitor/Nexodose environment will require that it interfaces upon conversion, bidirectionally with the site's electronic health record (Oracle Health/Cerner) via HL7 messaging to support orders and results exchange, and includes an outbound API/HL7 feed for downstream data consumption. Continued annual maintenance and support (M&S) is required to sustain system availability, vendor-supplied upgrades/updates, and interface reliability across the Production and Test environments. 2. PURPOSE / SCOPE The Contractor shall provide annual software maintenance and support for the DoseMonitor/Nexodose platform, the outbound API/HL7 interface, and the bi-directional HL7 interfaces between DoseMonitor/Nexodose and the site's Cerner environment (both Production and Test instances), and shall perform one-time installation/configuration of the bi-directional Cerner HL7 interfaces in both the Production and Test environments, in accordance with the Contract Line Item Numbers (CLINs) identified in Section 4 below. This SOW covers a base period of performance and one (1) option period, as detailed in Section 5. 3. APPLICABLE DOCUMENTS The Contractor shall perform all work in accordance with: VA Handbook 6500 and applicable VA Information Security requirements HIPAA Privacy and Security Rules (45 CFR Parts 160, 164) Health Level Seven (HL7) v2.x messaging standards, as applicable to the interfaces described herein Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act (accessibility standards), where applicable to any software deliverables VA Directive 6102, VA Enterprise Architecture, and applicable VISN / facility local IT and Biomedical Engineering policies Manufacturer/vendor technical specifications for DoseMonitor/Nexodose 4. CONTRACT LINE ITEMS (CLINs) AND TASK REQUIREMENTS CLIN Description Qty/UOM DM-10-KAN-BY-AM&S � DoseMonitor/Nexodose Annual Maintenance & Support 1 EA DM-10-KAN-BY-OB � Outbound API/HL7 Annual Maintenance & Support 2 EA DM-10-KAN-BY-CERNER PRO � Bi-Directional (Orders/Results) HL7 Interface to Cerner, PRODUCTION 1 EA DM-10-KAN-BY-CERN-HL7-P � Bi-Directional Interface, Cerner PRODUCTION, Annual M&S (includes all upgrades/updates) 1 EA DM-10-KAN-BY-CERNER TEST � Bi-Directional (Orders/Results) HL7 Interface to Cerner, TEST 1 EA DM-10-KAN-BY-CERN-HL7-T � Bi-Directional Interface, Cerner TEST, Annual M&S (includes all upgrades/updates) 1 EA Base Period Total: 4.1 CLIN 0001 � DoseMonitor/Nexodose Annual Maintenance & Support The Contractor shall provide annual software maintenance and technical support for the DoseMonitor/Nexodose application, to include: Access to a technical support/help desk during standard business hours (minimum 8:00 AM � 5:00 PM local facility time, Monday�Friday, excluding federal holidays), with a defined escalation path for critical (system-down) issues. All vendor-issued software updates, patches, and version upgrades released during the period of performance, at no additional cost. Remote diagnostic and troubleshooting support for software defects, performance issues, and configuration errors. Proactive notification of known issues, security patches, and end-of-life/end-of-support milestones affecting the software. Software license renewal/maintenance to ensure continued authorized use of the application for the period of performance. 4.2 CLIN 0002 � Outbound API/HL7 Annual Maintenance & Support The Contractor shall provide annual maintenance and support for the outbound API/HL7 interface(s) used to export dose-tracking data from DoseMonitor/Nexodose to downstream consuming systems, to include: Monitoring and support of outbound message transmission to ensure data integrity and timely delivery. Troubleshooting and remediation of interface errors, message failures, or mapping issues. Support for any vendor-side configuration changes required due to upgrades to the DoseMonitor/Nexodose platform. Documentation of the outbound interface specification, updated as changes occur. 4.3 CLIN 0003 � Bi-Directional HL7 Interface to Cerner, PRODUCTION (One-Time Installation) The Contractor shall design, configure, install, and validate a bi-directional HL7 interface between DoseMonitor/Nexodose and the facility's Cerner Production environment to support orders and results exchange, to include: Interface build and configuration in coordination with facility Biomedical Engineering, Radiology, and Health Informatics/IT staff. HL7 message mapping (e.g., ORM/ORU or applicable message types) between DoseMonitor/Nexodose and Cerner. End-to-end interface testing and validation in the Production environment prior to go-live, including a documented test plan and results. Coordination of a go-live/cutover date with facility stakeholders and the VA Interface Team. Delivery of as-built interface documentation, including message specifications and data mapping. 4.4 CLIN 0004 � Bi-Directional Interface, Cerner PRODUCTION, Annual Maintenance & Support Following successful installation under CLIN 0003, the Contractor shall provide annual maintenance and support for the Production bi-directional HL7 interface, to include: All upgrades and updates to the interface engine/configuration required to maintain compatibility with DoseMonitor/Nexodose and Cerner throughout the period of performance. Ongoing interface monitoring support and troubleshooting of message failures or data discrepancies. Support for interface re-validation following any Cerner or DoseMonitor/Nexodose upgrade

title: Unison Proposers Day Announcement
description: PROPOSERS DAY: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) Strategic Technology Office (STO) will host a Proposers Day in support of DARPA-PS-27-06, Unison program, on 5 November 2026 at the System Planning and Analysis Research Collaboration Center (SPARCC), 4075 Wilson Blvd., Suite 201 from 9:00AM-2:00 PM EST. The purpose of this conference is to provide information on the Unison program; promote additional discussion on this topic; address questions from potential proposers; and provide a forum for potential proposers to meet potential teaming partners. PROGRAM OBJECTIVE AND DESCRIPTION: The objective of the Unison program is to develop and evaluate collaborative-autonomy approaches that jointly adapt team decision-making and communications during mission execution. Unison will investigate approaches that enable autonomous teams to modify tactics, behaviors, coordination relationships, and information exchange as mission complexity and operational variability increase and communications become extremely constrained and/or degraded.

title: USMCFP SPRINGFIELD - Bio-Medical Waste Removal
description: Completed SF1449 is required with bid and bid must be within spec of the Statement of Work to be considered. USMCFP SPRINGFIELD MEDICAL WASTE DISPOSAL: STATEMENT OF WORK Subject The Federal Bureau of Prisons intends to make a single award to a responsible entity for the provision of Medical Waste Disposal for USMCFP Springfield. Medical Waste Disposal services shall only be used for medical hazardous waste that cannot be disposed of with garbage removed by the standard trash service. This contract is for Medical Waste Disposal that will need to be provided every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday throughout the contract. Place of Performance Services for Medical Waste Disposal will be performed at the address 1900 W Sunshine St. Springfield, Missouri 65807. There is a commercial entrance off Sunshine Steet to access the property. The driver will proceed to the talk box and receive directions from the officer. There is a small structure that houses medical waste. Period of Performance USMCFP Springfield is soliciting for a 12-month period of performance to start date of award and end 12 months after date of award with a 6-month option to extend to 18 months after date of original award. Schedule The contractor shall pick up Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays for the duration of the contract. Any deviation from this schedule will be mutually agreed upon by the Contractor and the Government. There will be no pickups on federal holidays. Pickups scheduled for federal holidays will be rescheduled for the next business day. Note: Three pickups will be required each week per policy. The time of pick up will be from 7:30 am to 10:30 am or 11:30 am to 2:30 pm. Licensing Requirements The institution requires all applicable Federal, EPA, and Missouri licensing / regulations that are standard for this industry. Service must also comply with the Disposal of Patient Materials standards which I have attached below: Security Clearance Services will be provided outside the secured confines of the institution. Please see the Terms and Conditions for any further requirements. Description of Duties The objective of this contract is to provide Medical Waste Disposal for USMCFP Springfield. The contractor shall be responsible for, but is not limited to, the following: The contractor shall be responsible for the collection, removal, and disposal of infectious medical waste. These duties must be in accordance with all Federal, State, City ordinances, laws, and regulations. Containers to furnish will be red, reusable plastic tubs with lid with overall dimensions of not to exceed (24x24x24 inches). Preferably 31 Gallon in size tubs. Tub liners and tape will be furnished by the contractor and appropriately supplied with each pickup. The contractor will leave an appropriate number of tubs and lids to exchange upon request. This includes providing properly sanitized tubs and lids. The contractor holder will determine an appropriate quantity of tubs to have on hand. On average 8 full tubs will be picked up Monday�s and Wednesday�s. Fridays will average 16-20 full tubs. The estimated medical waste to be removed is 85,000 lbs per year. Only the actual weight of waste collected will be billed. Disposal charge does not include the weight of the reusable tubs or lids. Electronic manifest is preferred Each Invoice will contain: Date of pickup, number of pickups, total weight of waste picked up, pricing according to the contract mirroring the line items on the contract. Point of Contact Contractor shall provide a Point of Contact (POC) who shall be responsible for the delivery of the services under this contract. The POC shall have the full authority to act on behalf of the contractor on all matters relating to the daily operation of the contracted services. The contractor shall designate this individual, in writing, to the Contracting Officer (CO) prior to contract start date. An alternate may be designated; however, the contractor must identify those times when the alternate shall be the primary POC. English Language Requirements The contractor performing the services under this contractual agreement shall have the ability to read, understand, fluently speak and legibly write in the English language. Government Quality Assurance The Government reserves the right to inspect and evaluate all services provided during the performance under this contract. All observations will be documented by the designated Contracting Officer�s Representative (COR). When an observation indicates defective performance, the Contracting Officer, along with the support of the COR, may issue a Discrepancy Report to the contractor. The contractor shall address any Discrepancy Report in writing to the COR and the Contracting Officer, within ten (10) calendar days of notification indicating any corrective action to be taken to rectify the deficiency. Non-Personal Services Information The service is a contractual arrangement and not a personnel appointment. Payment is based on the provision of an end product or the accomplishment of a specific result. The service does not constitute an employer/employee relationship.

title: Kingdom of Bahrain S&RTS
description: The purpose of this requirement is to provide S&RTS in connection with the import and export of designated U.S. Government (USG) cargo throughout the Kingdom of Bahrain. Primary performance locations include Mina Salman Port, Khalifa Bin Salman Port, ASRY Dry Dock, Naval Support Activity (NSA1), Mina Salman Naval Base (NSA2), Shaikh Isa Air Base, Aviation Unit (NSA3), Riffa Air Base and any other designated locations within Kingdom of Bahrain. S&RTS services will cover the full spectrum of managing USG cargo (e.g. containers, vehicles, breakbulk, and rotary or fixed wing aircraft) transiting through the specified port(s) in this contract. Operational tasks shall include but are not limited to stevedoring and long-shoring services required to conduct and facilitate load and discharge of vessel, truck, port reception and disposition, cargo management and preparation, staging, storage, onward movement, intra-port transfers, vessel preparation, documentation, tallying and checking, and storage of dunnage and tiedown materials. Military cargo may consist of vehicles, Ammunition and Explosives (A&E) in all sizes and configurations (containerized or breakbulk), non-explosive containers of all sizes, all classes of Hazardous Materials (HAZMAT) (IAW applicable regulations), and other general DoW cargo. Transportation will be facilitated via vessel, Common-User Land Transportation (CULT), and/or military convoy.

title: NAWCAD WOLF Tactical Voice Conferencing System (TVCS) Basic Ordering Agreement Task Order - 3
description: The Government intends to award a firm-fixed-price contract to Cornet Technology, Inc. as a sole-source (other than full and open competition) Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) task order. This requirement is for the organic Lead Systems Integrator (oLSI) for the Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWCAD), Webster Outlying Field (WOLF) operating under a product-based business model whereby NAWCAD WOLF civilians lead and manage the execution of the requirements with combined Government-Industry teams. Using this oLSI approach, the Government maintains control of intellectual property and data rights, enabling WOLF to rapidly adapt solutions to the dynamic needs of the warfighter. This requirement is for integration and installation, testing, site support, hardware and software maintenance, training, and hardware for the Tactical Voice Conferencing System (TVCS) OMNI system. The TVCS OMNI system, a replacement to the TVCS mid-range (MR) end-of-life system, is a Marine Corps Risk Management Framework (RMF) accredited communications, conferencing, and interconnect solution that provides radio and telephone conferencing functionality. The TVCS OMNI system fulfills a vital role in Command, Control, Communications, Military Air Management Control, and Mission Control. The function and purpose of the TVCS OMNI system is to provide Marine Corps Range Operators with secure and non-secure sea, air, and ground communications as well as the ability to communicate across networks with both secure and non-secure radios and telephones with carrier-class reliability. This acquisition is being pursued on a sole source basis under the statutory authority of Title 10, U.S.C. Section 3204(a) (1), as implemented by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.103-1, Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. A determination by the Government not to compete this effort is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information provided herein is subject to change and in no way binds the Government to solicit for or award a contract, or to be responsible for any monies expended by any interested parties before award of a contract for the effort described above. This notice of intent is neither a request for proposal nor a solicitation of offers. This synopsis is provided for information purposes only. A determination not to compete this requirement is solely within the discretion of the United States Government. For subcontracting opportunities, please visit Cornets website at:https://cornet.com/

description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE FOR INDEFINITE DELIVERY/INDEFINITE QUANTITY (IDIQ) MULTIPLE AWARD CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT (MACC) FOR MINOR GENERAL CONSTRUCTION AT NAVAL SUPPORT ACTIVITY (NSA) CRANE, INDIANA AND GLENDORA TEST FACILITY SULLIVAN, INDIANA THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. The intent of this notice is to conduct market research to determine if sources capable of satisfying this agency�s requirements exist. The Naval Facilities Engineering Command (NAVFAC), Mid-Atlantic is seeking eligible Small Business firms capable of performing minor construction services for Naval Support Activity (NSA) Crane located in Crane, Indiana and the Glendora Test Facility located in Sullivan, Indiana. Work may be required in other areas in the area of responsibility of NAVFAC Mid-Atlantic and NAVFAC Atlantic if deemed necessary and approved by the NAVFAC Mid-Atlantic Chief of the Contracting Office. Large business submittals will not be considered. The Government is not obligated to and will not pay for any information received from potential sources as a result of this synopsis. The information provided in this notice is subject to change and in no way binds the Government to solicit for or award a contract. No drawings or specifications will be made available at this time. The Government will not provide debriefs on the results of this research, but feedback regarding the decision to set aside or not set aside the procurement will be accomplished via pre-solicitation synopsis or solicitation for these services, as applicable. All information submitted will be held in a confidential manner and will only be used for the purpose intended. This contract(s) will require the ability to manage multiple task orders concurrently across NSA Crane and the Glendora Test Facility. There is a possibility that projects at remote Military Reserve Centers up to 250 miles from NSA Crane may be offered, however, a vast majority of the work will be performed at NSA Crane. This MACC will encompass a wide range of projects that include, but are not limited to, demolition, repair, replacement, modification, and renovation of buildings, systems and infrastructure for various facilities. Types of facilities may include, but are not limited to, administrative, industrial, warehouses, maintenance, communications, schools/training/education, personnel support, recreational, food services, lodging, medical, training areas/ranges, roads, etc. Work with specialty trades includes Mechanical/Electrical/Plumbing (MEP) systems including Heating Ventilating and Air Conditioning (HVAC) systems, boilers, high pressure steam distribution, electrical distribution, motors, generators, potable water distribution, sanitary sewer, storm water control, communications, and removal and disposal of asbestos or lead contaminated materials will also be required. title: Subscription to a Mathematical Bibliographic and Expert Reviews Database
description: BACKGROUND The NIST Research Library and Museum (Library) within Management Resources (MR), provides scientific and technical information assistance to 3,100 full-time staff and 2,000 researchers across the Gaithersburg, MD, and Boulder, CO campuses. To support NIST�s measurement science mission, the Library delivers access to critical electronic resources, including technical publications, e-journals, e-books, and scientific databases. Due to the volume and technical complexity of global mathematical literature, NIST researchers require specialized indexing, abstracting, and peer-critiqued evaluation tools. This acquisition provides campus-wide online access to a mathematical bibliographic and expert review database to enable efficient evaluation of proof validity, citation tracking, and discovery of peer-reviewed mathematical findings. By facilitating global information discovery, access, and digital resource management, the Library ensures researchers maintain rigorous scientific integrity and technical leadership. NIST has a requirement to provide campus-wide access to a mathematical bibliographic and expert review database. Due to the volume and technical complexity of global mathematical literature, NIST researchers require specialized indexing, abstracting, and peer-critiqued evaluation tools. The Library requires campus-wide online access to a curated mathematics bibliographic and expert review database. Access ensures researchers can evaluate proof validity, trace citation history, and discover relevant peer-reviewed findings efficiently. NIST has not yet determined its acquisition strategy for this requirement and encourages interested sources to respond to this Notice. See attached document for specific details and instructions. QUESTIONS ABOUT THIS NOTICE For additional information, please contact the primary contact identified at the bottom of this notice. THANK YOU Thank you for taking the time to read this notice and for your interest in helping NIST with its efforts to maximize competition!

description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL OR INVITATION FOR BID. THERE WILL NOT BE A SOLICITATION, SPECIFICATIONS OR DRAWINGS AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME. The intent of this notice is to conduct market research to determine if sources capable of satisfying this agency�s requirements exist. This MACC will encompass a wide range of DB and DBB projects that include, but are not limited to, demolition, repair, replacement, modification, new construction, and renovation of buildings, systems and infrastructure for various facilities. title: Support sustainment of Naval Weapon Systems and Platforms operating beyond their projected service lives.
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION. This is a Request for Information (RFI) issued by Naval Supply Systems Command (NAVSUP) Fleet Logistics Center (FLC) Norfolk, Regional Directorate-Mechanicsburg, PA on behalf of the NAVSUP WSS personnel supporting naval weapon-system sustainment activities at the Philadelphia and Mechanicsburg locations. The Fleet Logistics Center Norfolk, Regional Directorate-Mechanicsburg, PA Office is seeking marketing information, from responsible sources to gain knowledge of potential qualified business sources capable of providing the following services in the attached draft Statement of Work (SOW). NAVSUP WSS has a requirement to procure and to obtain services identified in the attached Draft SOW to provide required access to a commercially available, web-based parts and materials database to support sustainment of Naval Weapon Systems and Platforms operating beyond their projected service lives. A qualified vendor must have access to GIDEP (Government Industry Data Exchange Program) and to FAA databases used to identify and manage obsolescence and counterfeit material avoidance can satisfy this requirement. NAVSUP WSS has determined that the ability to obtain parts through a database that can cross reference military and commercial elements, consolidate information from diverse sources, connect to GIDEP (Government Industry Data Exchange Program) and to FAA databases used to identify and manage obsolescence and counterfeit material avoidance is indispensable to meet its mission requirements. In addition, provide supplier verification (ensure supplier is not on the Federal Debarment List, addresses are correct, origin registration, and applicable certificates), ensuring the stock listed by the suppliers are accurate and updated, provide companies in accordance with the government supplier listing program, provide a government research tool, and provide NATO national stock number data. The resultant contract will require Contractor must possess the ability to access the GIDEP (Government Industry Data Exchange Program) and to FAA databases at time of the quote submission, and must maintain the level of access to GIDEP and to FAA databases for the life of the contract. The Base period of performance (POP) is from 16 March 2027 through 15 March 2028 with four (4) Options if exercised would have an ending POP date of 15 February 2032. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code is 541519 and the small business standard is $34,000,000.00. Included with this Sources Sought Notice (RFI) are the draft Statement of Work (SOW) associated with this effort for reference when responding to this RFI. Firms offering the requisite skills, resources and capabilities necessary to perform the stated requirement are invited to respond to this RFI providing industry feedback to the draft PWS. Submissions are not to exceed two (2) typewritten WORD document pages in no less than 12 font size. All comments/ideas will be considered, although any questions/comments/ideas will not be responded to directly. The goal of such feedback is to consider suggestions that might enhance competition, improve the clarity of the requirement, or leverage industry expertise, as well as any other ideas that could result in improved services. The submission should include the following information and reference N0018927QW009: Company name, address, and point of contact with corresponding phone number and e-mail address DUNS number, Cage Code, Business Size and Classification, NAICS Code# for this Service Requirement An indication if any service is available under your GSA Schedule Any information that is an industry standard and not particular to your company including performance standards and/or practices that may be considered for this requirement. Please provide if your company can perform to the period of performance with Options until the requirement completion. Please reply: Does your Company have access to both GIDEP and to FAA databases for the life of the contract: Access to GIDEP Database: Yes _____ or No_______ Access to FAA Database: Yes _____ or No_______ (Vendor must maintain access to the GIDEP and to FAA databases for the life of the contract. The Base period of performance (POP) is from 16 March 2027 through 15 March 2028 with four (4) Options if exercised would have an ending POP date of 15 February 2032.) This is not a notice of solicitation. This RFI does not constitute an RFP, nor does this issuance restrict the Government's acquisition approach. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, catalog, or service specifications which shall be considered by the FLC Norfolk Regional Directorate-Mechanicsburg, PA. title: J--FIRE AND SECURITY ALARM MONITORING SERVICES FOR GO
description: THIS AMENDMENT TO SOURCES SOUGHT IS TO ADD LIST OF CURRENT EQUIPMENT. NATIONAL PARK SERVICE Golden Gate National Recreation Area (GGNRA), San Francisco County, California FIRE AND SECURITY ALARM MONITORING SERVICES FOR GOLDEN GATE NATIONAL RECREATION AREA SOURCES SOUGHT 140PP027Q0017 1. Introduction: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT ANNOUNCEMENT ONLY- This Source Sought is solely for information and planning, as a means for the government to conduct market research, identifying interested parties and their capability to support the requirements for fire and security alarm monitoring equipment and services for NPS-occupied buildings in GGNRA. Golden Gate National Recreation Area (GGNRA) encompasses over 80,000 acres spanning three counties, and includes over 700 historic and non-historic structures. Many of these structures are NPS- and partner-occupied buildings. In accordance with NPS policies, these buildings must be monitored for life safety via fire alarm systems. Most occupied buildings also have security alarms. Currently, alarm responses are overseen by the NPS Communications Center (Dispatch), located in the Presidio of San Francisco. The Dispatch receiving station is owned by NPS and operated by the United States Park Police. All NPS-occupied buildings are solely monitored by Dispatch. Partners may use third-party monitoring agencies for security only, but fire alarms currently report to NPS Dispatch. Per the 2026 Condition Assessment, the current monitoring system, both hardware and software, is fully obsolete. The park has determined that a third-party monitoring system is preferred, to ensure that hardware and software are maintained by subject matter experts: NPS Dispatch will serve as an ancillary receiving station. Also, park partners will no longer be required to report fire alarms directly to Dispatch: both fire and security alarms may be monitored by third parties, so long as notifications are also sent to NPS Dispatch. There are approximately 110 GGNRA/NPS-occupied buildings which will require monitoring. NPS anticipates that existing alarm control panels in good condition can be maintained / reused, and that new communications units will need to be installed and monitored by a third-party vendor. POTS lines are being terminated in the park. The park is neutral regarding the type(s) of communications units, which may radio alarm transmitters, include cellular service, or satellite: note that there are topographic challenges to communications in the park which will need to be addressed by the future vendor, particularly in Marin County. Responses to this Sources Sought will be considered and will help the Government dictate a path forward. All business categories will be considered to include small and large businesses. 2. Place of Performance: Golden Gate National Recreation Area (GGNRA), San Francisco County, California. 3. Disclaimer: This notice does not obligate the Government to award a contract or otherwise pay for the information provided in response. An organization responding to this notice should ensure that its response is complete and sufficiently detailed to allow the Government to determine the organization's qualifications to perform the work. Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge the information received or provide feedback to respondents with respect to any information submitted. After a review of the responses received, a pre- solicitation synopsis and solicitation may be published online at the Contract Opportunities website at www.sam.gov. Responses to this notice will not be considered adequate responses to a solicitation. 4. Contractor Capability: Provide all supervision, labor, materials, and equipment necessary to support the requirements for fire and security alarm monitoring equipment and services for NPS-occupied buildings in GGNRA. Basic Description of Work: � The contractor shall provide all manpower, equipment, and supplies to perform the requested services. � The contractor shall perform continuous monitoring of fire and security alarms with alerts transmitted to appropriate responders, including San Francisco Fire Department, Marin County Fire Department, Southern Marin Fire Department, and National Park Service Communications Center (United States Park Police and NPS Law Enforcement) in accordance with NFPA 72 National Fire Alarm and Signaling Code, and NPS Director�s Order & Reference Manual 28 Structural Fire Management. Identify any other national codes applicable to the process (International Code Council, National Fire Protection Association, et al.) � Purchase or lease of new communications units for fire, security and/or hybrid control panels at approximately 110 buildings [lease preferred]. � Operations and maintenance of monitoring and communications elements, including hardware and software updates as needed. � Installation requirements for new equipment and proposed installation process (by offeror or others). Installations shall comply with the International Fire Code, International Electrical Code, NFPA 70 and NFPA 72. Note that existing power supply and conduit shall be used to the maximum extent feasible. � Initial commissioning and regular testing, inspection and maintenance (ITM) of the equipment. � Vendors must comply with FAR clause 52.204-25, Prohibition on Contracting for Certain Telecommunications and Video Surveillance Services or Equipment. Contractor shall perform the following services � Continuous monitoring of fire and security alarms, with simultaneous notification to first responders and NPS law enforcement � Maintain communications units and receiving station(s) in operable condition, in accordance with annual testing, inspection and maintenance requirements per NFPA 72 and NPS Reference Manual 58 � Address malfunctioning / inoperable fire alarm equipment within [24 hours] in accordance with NFPA 72 code requirements � Address malfunctioning / inoperable security alarm equipment within [72 hours] in accordance with NPS policies � Perform quality control activities and provide [monthly] status reports to NPS regarding [alarms received and type, responders contacted, number of units in operation, number of malfunctions / inoperable units, number of repairs made and duration to restore to operation] 5. Response to Sources Sought: Interested contractors must be currently registered (or be able to register prior to any future award) in the System for Award Management (SAM) at the official SAM website at www.sam.gov (SAM registration is FREE - there is no cost to use SAM). Interested contractors able to perform the type of work detailed above are encouraged to PROVIDE THEIR COMPANY OR ENTITY NAME, ADDRESS, Unique Entity ID NUMBER, CONTACT INFORMATION (phone and email) FOR PRIMARY POINTS OF CONTACT. Additional information to provide: 1. Your Company�s Business Size 2. Relevant Information demonstrating capability to perform this type of work. Include sample projects that are like this requirement including estimated costs of the project performed. 3. The communication equipment does your company offer for lease or for purchase? 4. Do you have service contracts that are similar work for base and Option Years? If so, please provide a sample. Email Responses directly to Contracting Officer Liset Gomez at liset_gomez@ios.doi.gov. Any questions can be directed to Liset Gomez via email or by telephone at 415-265-5650. Responses are due no later than October 29,2026 at 12:00pm Pacific Time. 6. Important Notes: Interested parties may register at www.sam.gov to receive notification when the solicitation and any amendments or notices are issued and available for downloading. Please note that the General Services Administration provides the notification service as a convenience and does not guarantee that notifications will be received by all persons on the mailing list. Therefore, we recommend that you monitor the Contracting Opportunities site at

The project consists of replacing the existing bridge with a new fixed bridge on a new alignment and to provide for partial demolition of the existing bridge. The bridge width will be 34�4�� out-to-out, with two 11�0� travel lanes, two 2�0� shoulders, a 5�0� sidewalk, and the superstructure will consist of four (4) built-up steel plate girders. The existing bridge provides for critical vehicular access to the Bonneville project that must remain open for the entirety of the construction project. This will likely require the contractor to construct the project in phases. In addition, lead and asbestos removal will be required as part of this requirement. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) � Southwestern Division(SWD) is conducting market research to determine the interest and capability of firms to submit Standard Form 330 (SF-330) Architect-Engineer Qualifications statements for an eight-year $499M indefinite delivery contract(s) (IDC). The decision of whether or not to include any type of set-aside or reserve within the IDC pool will depend upon the responses to this sources sought announcement and associated market research. The purpose of this sources sought notice is to gain knowledge of interest, capabilities and qualifications of various members of industry, to include the Small Business Community: Small Business, Section 8(a), Historically Underutilized Business Zones (HUB-Zone), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), and Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB), as well as Unrestricted Businesses. Small businesses, Section 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, and WOSB businesses are highly encouraged to participate. Project Scope: A full range of A-E services for engineering and design are anticipated, which may include, but are not limited to any or all of the following: program management, data management, project programming and planning, feasibility and concept studies, space utilization, design concepts/standards, research, analysis, engineering, design, design/build request for proposal preparation, and engineering during construction for military, civil works and interagency services. Engineering and design within these services also include, but are not limited to, design of new construction, vertical and horizontal, alteration of facilities, maintenance and repair of real property, pre-design site assessment, topographic and boundary surveys to include mapping, geotechnical investigation and reports, environmental investigations, studies and reports, hazardous materials testing, abatement and monitoring, historical and cultural resource investigations, seismic studies, cost estimates, value engineering, design reviews, life cycle costing, computer aided drafting, geospatial information systems (GIS), and building information modeling (BIM). Engineering during construction includes responses to requests for information from construction contractors, post design-shop drawing review, and as-built review. The contractor(s) is also required to have expertise and knowledge of the following: Guiding Principles Assessment and Compliance Program for Department of Defense, DOW HPSB Checklist for self-certification; Federal Asbestos Hazard Emergency Response Act (AHERA) inspections and documentation; the design of Anti-Terrorism/Force Protection (AT/FP) requirements; security, data, and communications systems; fire protection and life safety systems; blast design; mechanical systems and commissioning; and other technical services that may be required. Typical vertical design includes site/civil engineering, structural engineering, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering and architecture. title: Head Start in State Systems Sole Source Award
description: This requirement was awarded through task order 47QRAA-20D-001M/7571MN26F80105 This requirement will support the generation and dissemination of research and/or evaluation that builds on the Financing Early Care and Education (ECE) Study task order (47QRAA-20D-001M/ 140D0422F0154). The primary objective is to generate and disseminate evidence pertaining to the financing of early care and education programs that meet child, family, and community needs. Building on data collected under the prior contract, this project will identify and elevate strategies used to align Head Start programs within state funding contexts to reduce administrative burden and expand the reach of ECE and Head Start funding. The research will focus on how Head Start programs operate within state systems and highlight effective strategies states have used to integrate or build upon Head Start funding within their broader early childhood systems. The project will also examine how efforts to streamline licensing and regulatory requirements, workforce standards, and supports for quality and technical assistance across funding streams can reduce burden, improve program efficiency, increase parental access to ECE, and support child and family outcomes. This requirement will build on prior efforts to identify and elevate financing approaches for states that most effectively align funding streams to both reduce burden and increase the reach of ECE funding. This project will provide ACF with critical evidence to understand how federal early care and education programs can achieve the Agency�s mission and vision of (1) supporting federalism & local leadership by providing actionable insights into how states and localities can leverage Head Start and other federal funding streams for early care and education (ECE) to best meet local needs, (2) promoting quality early learning environments and improved child outcomes by understanding how to leverage existing funding sources to best meet the preferences of families with young children consistent with their unique needs, and (3) promoting work and self-sufficiency by exploring how leveraging funds can expand the availability of ECE services that allow parents to work.

description: Pre-Solicitation Conference � NSWCPD Environmental Qualification Test Services The Naval Surface Warfare Center Philadelphia Division (NSWCPD) invites interested contractors to a pre-solicitation conference regarding the future requirement for Testing Services in support of Shock and Vibration and Electromagnetic Interference / Compatibility (EMI/EMC) Environmental Qualification efforts for Navy Hull, Mechanical, and Electrical (HME) equipment. This event is an opportunity for NSWCPD to inform industry partners about this upcoming need and to discuss potential strategies for meeting the demand. What: Pre-Solicitation Conference � NSWCPD Environmental Qualification Test Services When: 11/12/2026, 1230 - 1600 (In-person check-in: 1230-1300) Where: NSWCPD Philadelphia Navy Yard, Building 77L Room 200; 1000 Kitty Hawk Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19112. Free parking will be available. A parking map will be provided to registered attendees. A virtual meeting link will be provided to registered attendees no later than 11/9/2026. Why Attend? Learn about NSWCPD's FY27-32 requirement for Environmental Qualification Test Services in accordance with established Military Standards and Specifications. Discuss potential acquisition strategies and approaches to meet the anticipated demand for these services. Network to gain a greater insight into NSWCPD�s requirements. About Environmental Qualification Test Services: NSWCPD DEPARTMENT 30 conducts small to medium scale shock, vibration, and electromagnetic interference and electromagnetic compatibility (EMI/EMC) testing on shipboard and submarine hull, mechanical, and electrical (HME) equipment to reduce risks associated with new or updated equipment designs before they are installed on U.S. Navy ships. Within Department 30, Code 333 has authority to approve shock and vibration test plans, as well as EMI/EMC test plans, for ship and submarine HME equipment prior to the conduct of a test. title: Z2DA--FY27 NRM | 557-23-104 | Replace Boiler Plant Steam Boilers | Construction (VA-27-00003633)
description: NO PROPOSALS ARE BEING REQUESTED AT THIS TIME. THIS NOTICE SERVES AS THE PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE PRIOR TO ISSUANCE OF THE FORMAL SOLICITATION. DESCRIPTION: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Network Contracting Office 7, has a requirement for Project Number 557-23-104, Replace Boiler Plant Steam Boilers, at the Carl Vinson VA Medical Center in Dublin, Georgia. The contractor will provide management, supervision, materials, tools, and labor to replace three steam boilers in Building 27 at the Carl Vinson VAMC Dublin, Georgia. Work will include but is not limited to temporary boiler plant and control room, hazardous material abatement, demolition of existing plant equipment, piping, and electricity, installation of new plant equipment and piping, site work, fuel tank installation and piping, and emergency generator installation based on provided A/E design drawings and specifications. All work will be done in compliance with Federal, State, and local regulations and in accordance with all work in the specifications and drawings. TYPE OF CONTRACT AND NAICS: This acquisition will result in one (1) Firm Fixed Price Contract. The contract period of performance is anticipated to be Seven Hundred Thirty (730) calendar days from issuance of the Notice to Proceed (NTP). The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 236220-Commercial and Institutional Building Construction, with size standard of $45,000,000. TYPE OF SET-ASIDE: This acquisition is a 100% Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) competition. CONSTRUCTION MAGNITUDE: In accordance with VAAR 836.204, the magnitude of this construction project is anticipated to be between $20,000,000 and $50,000,000 and closer to the lower price. SELECTION PROCESS: The proposals will be evaluated using the Highest Technically Rated-Fair and Reasonable Price best value source selection process. This is a one-phase Design-Bid-Build procurement process. Evaluation Factors are anticipated to include Relevant Past Experience, Implementation Plan to include critical path, and a Fair and Reasonable Price. Pro Forma Information such as bonding and financial capability will also be required to meet the minimum requirements of the solicitation. DISCUSSIONS: The Government intends to award without discussions but reserves the right to conduct discussion should it be deemed in the Government's best interest. Actual dates and times will be identified in the solicitation. Additional details can be found in the solicitation when it is posted. No requests for information will be addressed at this time. SITE VISIT: Site visit information will be posted with the solicitation. SOLICITATION WEBSITE: The official solicitation, when posted, will be available free of charge by electronic posting only and may be found at the System for Award Management (SAM) website, https://www.sam.gov. Paper copies of the solicitation will not be issued. Telephone and Fax requests for this solicitation will not be honored. To download the solicitation for this project, contractors are required to register at https://www.sam.gov. Amendments, if/when issued, will be posted to the above referenced website for electronic downloading. This will be the only method of distributing amendments prior to closing; therefore, it is the Offerors responsibility to check the website periodically for any amendments to the solicitation. REGISTRATIONS: Offerors shall have and shall maintain an active registration in the following database: System for Award Management (SAM): Offerors shall have and shall maintain an active registration in the SAM database at https://www.sam.gov to be eligible for a Government contract award. title: P1050 MAINTENANCE HANGAR AT NAS JRB FORT WORTH, TX.
description: PRE-SOLICITATION SYNOPSIS NOTICE ONLY: THE SOLICITATION WILL BE AVAILABLE ON OR ABOUT OCTOBER 29, 2026 AT HTTPS://SAM.GOV/. THE SOLICITATION NUMBER IS N6945027R0004, FOR THE DESIGN-BID-BUILD (DBB) CONSTRUCTION PROJECT FOR P1050 MAINTENANCE HANGAR LOCATED AT NAVAL AIR STATION (NAS) JOINT RESERVE BASE (JRB) FORT WORTH, TEXAS PROJECT TITLE: DESIGN BID BUILD CONSTRUCTION PROJECT, P1050 MAINTENANCE HANGAR LOCATED AT NAVAL AIR STATION (NAS) JOINT RESERVE BASE (JRB) FORT WORTH, TEXAS PSC: Z2BZ (Repair or Alteration of Other Airfield Structures) NAICS: 236220 � Commercial and Institutional Building Construction THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS OR AN INVITATION FOR BID. NO CONTRACT WILL BE AWARDED FROM THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO REIMBURSEMENT WILL BE MADE FOR ANY COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH PROVIDING INFORMATION IN RESPONSE TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT OR ANY FOLLOW-UP INFORMATION REQUESTS. No telephone calls will be accepted requesting a bid package or solicitation. There is no bid package or solicitation currently available. In order to protect the procurement integrity of any future procurement that may arise from this announcement, information regarding the technical point of contact will not be given and no appointments for presentations will be made. Description: This acquisition may result in the award of a Design Bid Build (DBB) Firm Fixed Price (FFP) Construction contract. for the renovation of a Maintenance Hangar at NAS JRB Fort Worth, Texas. The project consists of a two phased renovation of the interior and exterior of hangar 1050 including four separate interior admin spaces to better accommodate Marine Corps flight crews, equipment, and maintenance spaces for KC-130 and C-40 airframes. During renovation of Phase 1 spaces, aircraft maintenance operations will continue in Phase 2 areas. Similarly, when renovation continues into Phase 2 spaces, Phase 1 will be reoccupied and actively used for maintenance. Interior renovations encompass repair and replacement of all finishes, mechanical systems, plumbing, electrical, lighting, wet pipe fire suppression and fire alarm/mass notification systems. Exterior renovations include refinishing and repairing of the hangar doors and egress components and replacement of the hangar roof. Hangar bay renovation includes new electrical distribution, water distribution, waste water distribution, fire suppression, epoxy floor coating, compressed air system, heating and ventilation system and replacement of existing maintenance cranes and support railing. The contract performance period is 1,190 calendar days (inclusive of the base period and any exercised options) from the date of contract award. Schedule submission and progress tracking will be governed by FAR Clause 52.236-15, Schedules for Construction Contracts. The best value continuum source selection process to be used for this acquisition is the Tradeoff process in accordance with FAR 15.103-1. The Tradeoff process is appropriate when it may be in the best interest of the Government to consider award to other than the lowest priced offeror or other than the highest technically rated offeror. A sources sought notice was posted to sam.gov on July 1, 2026, requesting small business industry interested and capability statement. Based on responses from the notice it was determined that the requirement should be issued as Full and Open competition. The NAVFAC Small Business Office Concurs with this determination. The solicitation will be a negotiated DBB acquisition. Proposals will be solicited in a one-phase submission for a single solicitation. The solicitation will utilize source selection procedures, which require offerors to submit a technical proposal, past performance and experience information, and a price proposal for evaluation by the Government. Award will be made to the offeror whose total price and technical proposal offers the best value to the Government. Competition Requirements: Unrestricted basis, under full and open competition. Procurement Method: FAR Part 15, Contracting by Negotiation. Type of Contract: Firm-Fixed Price The NAICS code for this construction solicitation is 236220 with a size standard of $45,000,000. Project Magnitude is $90,000,000 or greater. This is a new procurement. It does not replace an existing contract. No prior contract information exists. A Site Visit will be held for those offerors who choose to participate (exact date and time will be specified in the solicitation). Proposals will be due no earlier than 30 days after the solicitation is released (exact date and time will be specified in the solicitation). This will be an electronic solicitation, which can be downloaded from Sam.gov Opportunities at https://sam.gov/. The solicitation will be available at this site no earlier than 15 days after this pre-solicitation notice is posted. Offerors are responsible for checking the Sam.gov website for the solicitation and any subsequent amendments that may be issued. NO CONTRACT AWARD WILL BE MADE TO ANY CONTRACTOR THAT IS NOT REGISTERED OR IN THE PROCESS OF REGISTERING WITH THE SYSTEM FOR AWARD MANAGEMENT (SAM). PLEASE VISIT THE SAM WEBSITE AT https://www.sam.gov FOR INSTRUCTIONS ON HOW TO REGISTER.

title: Q519--Research Support Psychological Assessment for PTSD Clinical Trial
description: Purpose The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is conducting market research in accordance with FAR Part 10 to determine the availability and capability of qualified small and large business concerns to provide psychological assessment services in support of a multi-site PTSD clinical research study. This notice is for market research purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation, request for proposal (RFP), or commitment by the Government to award a contract. Requirement Description The VA requires contractor support to provide independent psychological assessment services for participants enrolled in a multi-site clinical trial Hybrid Implementation and Non-Inferiority Testing of Group Versus Individual Written Exposure Therapy (WET) for posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD), in a group format compared to the established individual format.. The contractor shall provide qualified evaluators to conduct structured diagnostic assessments remotely with access to HIPAA-compliant Box so that contractor can receive participant contact information securely and can transmit interview scores securely back to VA. For more information on Box, please see https://digital.va.gov/marketplace/product/box/ Must also have access to HIPAA-complaint video conferencing for conducting the interviews themselves and must be overseen by PhD-level clinical psychologists to ensure ongoing high quality practice. Participants must complete standardized diagnostic assessments at baseline, post-treatment, and three-month follow-up. These assessments include the Clinician-Administered PTSD Scale for DSM-5 (CAPS-5) and the Mini International Neuropsychiatric Interview (MINI), both of which require administration by trained and qualified clinicians.. The anticipated effort includes approximately: 150 baseline CAPS-5 and MINI assessments 128 post-treatment CAPS-5 assessments 128 three-month follow-up CAPS-5 assessments Total projected assessments: approximately 414. Minimum Capability Requirements Interested firms should demonstrate their ability to: Provide master's- or doctoral-level clinicians trained in the administration of: Clinician-Administered PTSD Scale for DSM-5 (CAPS-5) Mini International Neuropsychiatric Interview (MINI) Recruit, train, supervise, and maintain an adequate pool of independent evaluators to support multiple research sites. Conduct assessments using HIPAA-compliant video conferencing technology. Securely receive and transmit participant information and assessment results using approved secure file-sharing platforms. Conduct quality assurance and fidelity monitoring activities to ensure consistency and reliability of assessments. Maintain compliance with applicable human subjects research requirements and regulatory training requirements. Provide oversight by doctoral-level clinical psychologists with expertise in PTSD assessment and diagnosis. Requested Information Interested vendors shall submit a capability statement not to exceed five (5) pages that includes: Company name, UEI, CAGE code, and business address. Business size and socioeconomic status under the applicable NAICS code(s). Experience providing psychological assessment services for: PTSD research studies Multi-site clinical trials Federal agencies Veterans or military populations Experience administering CAPS-5 and MINI assessments. Description of quality control and assessment fidelity procedures. Description of available staffing resources and evaluator qualifications. Recommended NAICS code(s) and rationale for why the code accurately describes the principal purpose of the requirement. Any existing contract vehicles available for ordering these services. NAICS Code The Government is considering the following NAICS codes: 621330, Offices of Mental Health Practitioners (except Physicians) 541990, All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services Respondents are encouraged to identify the NAICS code they believe best represents the principal purpose of the requirement and provide supporting rationale.
