title: J--FIRE AND SECURITY ALARM MONITORING SERVICES FOR GO
description: NATIONAL PARK SERVICE Golden Gate National Recreation Area (GGNRA), San Francisco County, California FIRE AND SECURITY ALARM MONITORING SERVICES FOR GOLDEN GATE NATIONAL RECREATION AREA SOURCES SOUGHT 140PP027Q0017 1. Introduction: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT ANNOUNCEMENT ONLY- This Source Sought is solely for information and planning, as a means for the government to conduct market research, identifying interested parties and their capability to support the requirements for fire and security alarm monitoring equipment and services for NPS-occupied buildings in GGNRA. Golden Gate National Recreation Area (GGNRA) encompasses over 80,000 acres spanning three counties, and includes over 700 historic and non-historic structures. Many of these structures are NPS- and partner-occupied buildings. In accordance with NPS policies, these buildings must be monitored for life safety via fire alarm systems. Most occupied buildings also have security alarms. Currently, alarm responses are overseen by the NPS Communications Center (Dispatch), located in the Presidio of San Francisco. The Dispatch receiving station is owned by NPS and operated by the United States Park Police. All NPS-occupied buildings are solely monitored by Dispatch. Partners may use third-party monitoring agencies for security only, but fire alarms currently report to NPS Dispatch. Per the 2026 Condition Assessment, the current monitoring system, both hardware and software, is fully obsolete. The park has determined that a third-party monitoring system is preferred, to ensure that hardware and software are maintained by subject matter experts: NPS Dispatch will serve as an ancillary receiving station. Also, park partners will no longer be required to report fire alarms directly to Dispatch: both fire and security alarms may be monitored by third parties, so long as notifications are also sent to NPS Dispatch. There are approximately 110 GGNRA/NPS-occupied buildings which will require monitoring. NPS anticipates that existing alarm control panels in good condition can be maintained / reused, and that new communications units will need to be installed and monitored by a third-party vendor. POTS lines are being terminated in the park. The park is neutral regarding the type(s) of communications units, which may radio alarm transmitters, include cellular service, or satellite: note that there are topographic challenges to communications in the park which will need to be addressed by the future vendor, particularly in Marin County. Responses to this Sources Sought will be considered and will help the Government dictate a path forward. All business categories will be considered to include small and large businesses. 2. Place of Performance: Golden Gate National Recreation Area (GGNRA), San Francisco County, California. 3. Disclaimer: This notice does not obligate the Government to award a contract or otherwise pay for the information provided in response. An organization responding to this notice should ensure that its response is complete and sufficiently detailed to allow the Government to determine the organization's qualifications to perform the work. Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge the information received or provide feedback to respondents with respect to any information submitted. After a review of the responses received, a pre- solicitation synopsis and solicitation may be published online at the Contract Opportunities website at www.sam.gov. Responses to this notice will not be considered adequate responses to a solicitation. 4. Contractor Capability: Provide all supervision, labor, materials, and equipment necessary to support the requirements for fire and security alarm monitoring equipment and services for NPS-occupied buildings in GGNRA. Basic Description of Work: � The contractor shall provide all manpower, equipment, and supplies to perform the requested services. � The contractor shall perform continuous monitoring of fire and security alarms with alerts transmitted to appropriate responders, including San Francisco Fire Department, Marin County Fire Department, Southern Marin Fire Department, and National Park Service Communications Center (United States Park Police and NPS Law Enforcement) in accordance with NFPA 72 National Fire Alarm and Signaling Code, and NPS Director�s Order & Reference Manual 28 Structural Fire Management. Identify any other national codes applicable to the process (International Code Council, National Fire Protection Association, et al.) � Purchase or lease of new communications units for fire, security and/or hybrid control panels at approximately 110 buildings [lease preferred]. � Operations and maintenance of monitoring and communications elements, including hardware and software updates as needed. � Installation requirements for new equipment and proposed installation process (by offeror or others). Installations shall comply with the International Fire Code, International Electrical Code, NFPA 70 and NFPA 72. Note that existing power supply and conduit shall be used to the maximum extent feasible. � Initial commissioning and regular testing, inspection and maintenance (ITM) of the equipment. � Vendors must comply with FAR clause 52.204-25, Prohibition on Contracting for Certain Telecommunications and Video Surveillance Services or Equipment. Contractor shall perform the following services � Continuous monitoring of fire and security alarms, with simultaneous notification to first responders and NPS law enforcement � Maintain communications units and receiving station(s) in operable condition, in accordance with annual testing, inspection and maintenance requirements per NFPA 72 and NPS Reference Manual 58 � Address malfunctioning / inoperable fire alarm equipment within [24 hours] in accordance with NFPA 72 code requirements � Address malfunctioning / inoperable security alarm equipment within [72 hours] in accordance with NPS policies � Perform quality control activities and provide [monthly] status reports to NPS regarding [alarms received and type, responders contacted, number of units in operation, number of malfunctions / inoperable units, number of repairs made and duration to restore to operation] 5. Response to Sources Sought: Interested contractors must be currently registered (or be able to register prior to any future award) in the System for Award Management (SAM) at the official SAM website at www.sam.gov (SAM registration is FREE - there is no cost to use SAM). Interested contractors able to perform the type of work detailed above are encouraged to PROVIDE THEIR COMPANY OR ENTITY NAME, ADDRESS, Unique Entity ID NUMBER, CONTACT INFORMATION (phone and email) FOR PRIMARY POINTS OF CONTACT. Additional information to provide: 1. Your Company�s Business Size 2. Relevant Information demonstrating capability to perform this type of work. Include sample projects that are like this requirement including estimated costs of the project performed. 3. The communication equipment does your company offer for lease or for purchase? 4. Do you have service contracts that are similar work for base and Option Years? If so, please provide a sample. Email Responses directly to Contracting Officer Liset Gomez at liset_gomez@ios.doi.gov. Any questions can be directed to Liset Gomez via email or by telephone at 415-265-5650. Responses are due no later than October 29,2026 at 12:00pm Pacific Time. 6. Important Notes: Interested parties may register at www.sam.gov to receive notification when the solicitation and any amendments or notices are issued and available for downloading. Please note that the General Services Administration provides the notification service as a convenience and does not guarantee that notifications will be received by all persons on the mailing list. title: Commercial Solution Opportunity - Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) CONUS
description: This is a Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) issued under the authority of DFARS 212.70. The Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) is focused on modernizing business operations by actively seeking innovative commercial technologies, products and services that will enhance our ability to deliver the military pay benefit at a significant patron savings. Authorized under DFARS Subpart 212-70, this CSO enables DeCA to competitively procure solutions through a streamlined acquisition process, allowing for rapid decisions. This approach underscores our mission to expedite the award and delivery of critical technologies, products, and services, ensuring that DeCA can leverage advancements in the grocery resale industry swiftly and efficiently. By prioritizing speed in our contracting efforts, we aim to support the timely integration of cutting-edge technologies, products, and services that enhance our ability to: improve the commissary benefit; decrease costs without diminishing the benefit; improve processes that have a high risk of potential fraud, waste, or abuse; and reduce waste and decrease variation in processes. Through this initiative, DeCA reaffirms its commitment to fostering innovation and enhancing business operations, ultimately delivering a vital benefit of the military compensation package that improves quality of life and readiness by providing grocery items at significant savings.

description: SYNOPSIS: INTRODUCTION: This Sources Sought Notice is for market research and information purposes only at this time and shall not be construed as a solicitation or as an obligation on the part of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA). This current project will also address the interconnection between the new and existing buildings. Minor modifications will also be necessary to the MRI building to maintain access/function during the construction of this project. Renovation of the existing PT space is not within the scope of this project. The Gross Square Footage (GSF) of the addition is estimated to be 14,080 GSF. PROCUREMENT INFORMATION: The proposed project will be a competitive, firm-fixed-price contract utilizing the design-bid-build approach (Final Specifications and Drawings will be provided). The anticipated solicitation will be issued either as a Request For Proposal (RFP) in accordance with FAR Part 15, considering Technical and Price Factors or as an Invitation for Bid (IFB) in accordance with FAR Part 14, considering Price only. The results and analysis of the market research will finalize the determination of the procurement method. The type of socio-economic set-aside, if any, will depend upon the responses to this notice and any other information gathered during the market research process. This project is planned for advertising in mid to late-December 2026. In accordance with VAAR 836.204, the magnitude of construction is between $10,000,000.00 and $20,000,000.00. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 236220 (size standard $45.0 million) applies to this procurement. The duration of the project is currently estimated at 550 calendar days from the issuance of a Notice to Proceed. The services for this project will include providing all construction related services such as: providing labor, materials and equipment required to complete the project as per contract documents prepared by an independent Architect-Engineer firm. CAPABILITY STATEMENT: Respondents shall provide a general capabilities statement to include the following information: Section 1: Provide company name, Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), company address, Point-of-Contact name, phone number and email. Section 2: Provide company business size based on NAICS code 236220. Also, provide business type (i.e., Large Business, Small Business, Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Business, Women-Owned Small Business, Hub Zone Small Business, etc.). Section 3: Provide a Statement of Interest in the project. Section 4: Provide the prime contractor s available bonding capacity in the form of a letter of intent from your bonding company with this submission. *Please ensure that the individual bonding capacity is in line with the VAAR Magnitude of Construction listed above. Section 5: Provide the type of work your company has performed in the past in support of the same or similar requirement. title: Market Intelligence: JDWC Progressive Design-Build OTA
description: (Please see attached Special Notice document W912HN27SA001 for full details and submission instructions). The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Savannah District, is issuing this Special Notice to conduct Market Intelligence for the Joint Deployment Warfighting Complex (JDWC) at Fort Bragg, North Carolina. This project will be procured utilizing a Progressive Design-Build (PDB) delivery method under the 10 U.S.C. 2808a Other Transaction (OT) authority for Construction. Project Snapshot: Scope: Design and construction of a high-security facility accommodating 750 personnel. Features include Secure Administrative Areas, Operations Centers, and SCIF spaces with stringent security requirements, along with fully redundant electrical/mechanical systems and major civil site modifications. Estimated Construction Budget: $350.0 Million. Acquisition Strategy: A streamlined, two-step Qualifications-Based Selection (QBS) process (Step 1: White Papers / Step 2: Pitch Meetings). Action Required: This is an Advance Notice for informational, planning, and market intelligence purposes only; it is not a formal Request for Proposal (RFP).Interested parties are requested to submit a capability statement (maximum of 5 pages) outlining their interest, bonding capacity, and relevant PDB and secure facility experience. Responses are due no later than October 29, 2026, at 4:00 PM Eastern Standard Time. All submissions must be electronic and emailed directly to the Points of Contact listed in the attached document. No hardcopy responses will be accepted.

title: CPMU - HRD Insertion Device
description: This pre-solicitation notice serves as a synopsis and is posted in accordance with FAR subpart 5.2, Synopses of Proposed Contract Actions. This is not a solicitation. Vendors shall not submit a quote until, and/or if, the solicitation is posted to the Governmentwide Point-of-Entry via www.SAM.gov. Vendors are not required to submit any response to this pre-solicitation notice. This announcement shall NOT be construed as a commitment by Brookhaven Science Associates LLC (BSA) to award a Subcontract. BSA reserves the right to use any and all information submitted by, or obtained from, an interested party in any manner BSA determines is appropriate, including, but not limited to, the creation of a solicitation. I. Background Brookhaven National Laboratory is a Department of Energy (DOE) National Laboratory multidisciplinary research facility, located on Long Island, New York. BSA intends to compete the subject requirement, to be utilized within the United States. This requirement will provide for full and open competition. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 335999, All Other Miscellaneous Electrical Equipment and Component Manufacturing (Size Standard, 600), and the applicable PSC is 6650, Optical Instruments, Test Equipment, Components and Accessories. Interested parties must be registered under the NAICS code in the System for Award Management (SAM) prior to submitting their proposal. BSA intends to issue a solicitation in support of this requirement by November 2026. BSA expects to make one (1) award. The anticipated award contract type is a firm-fixed price contract. At this time, BSA anticipates award date to be around February 2027. II. Description of Need BSA has the following requirement(s): The selected Contractor will be responsible for the for design, engineering, manufacturing, test, and delivery of the Cryogenic Permanent Magnet Undulator (CPMU) for the High Resolution Powder Diffraction (HRD) beamline. Please see the attached Statement of Work for more information. Delivery Date: 24 months after contract award

title: F/A-18 Fuel Pressure Gage Kit, P/N: 3867AS2060-1
description: AMENDMENT 0001: 19 October 2026 - Amendment 0001 hereby extends the solicitation closing date to 29 October 2026, 4:00pm EDT. Please submit all questions prior to 27 October 2026 for consideration and response. The Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWC-AD) is officially releasing a Request for Quote (RFQ) for a Firm Fixed Price (FFP) contract on a competitive basis for the procurement of Peculiar Support Equipment (PSE) as outlined in the attached Solicitation N68335-27-Q-1005 package: Evaluation Plan, Buy Terms and CLIN Structure. Technical Data Package and Export Control Requirements This solicitation includes DFARS 252.204-7025, Notice of Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) Requirements. The technical data package contains Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI). Offerors must obtain access to the CUI drawing package to prepare a proposal. Proof of CMMC Level 2 (self-assessment) certification is required to request access to the technical data package. The Government owns the Drawing Package for the Fuel Pressure Gage Kit, which is considered Export Controlled. All Offerors must possess a current and certified DD Form 2345 (Militarily Critical Technical Data Agreement) to request access to the drawings. Drawings will be provided to the designated data custodian listed on the certified DD Form 2345 via the DoD SAFE website. Requesting Access to Solicitation Documents To request access to the Government-provided documents associated with this solicitation, Offerors must submit the following via email: Proof of current and valid CMMC Level 2 (self-assessment) certification. A certified DD Form 2345. Requests should be sent to the Point of Contact (POC) listed below. Solicitation Number: N68335-27-Q-1005 Point of Contact and Questions The Point of Contact (POC) for this solicitation is: Mrs. Devin Hader, devin.l.hader.civ@us.navy.mil . All questions and inquiries regarding this solicitation must be submitted via email and reference Solicitation Number: N68335-27-Q-1005, Solicitation Title: F/A-18 Fuel Pressure Gage Kit. Questions must be received no later than 16:00 EST, 10/20/2026. Offerors are encouraged to review the Solicitation N68335-27-Q-1005 package thoroughly before submitting questions or requests for access. Late submissions of questions or requests for access may not be considered. This RFQ shall not be construed as obligating the Government to award a contract or authorizing work to commence and shall not serve as a basis for any future claims against the Government.

Reserves will be allocated for 8(a), HUBZone, Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB), and Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB). More detailed information regarding the Reserves is included in the solicitation document. PSC Code: Z2AA NAICS Code: 236220 Small Business Size Standard: $45M Description: This is a Multiple Award Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract that provides for an indefinite quantity of supplies or services during a fixed period. The GSA intends to award multiple contracts for General Construction Services. After award of the IDIQ all awardees will be provided fair opportunity in accordance with FAR 16.507-2 for discrete construction projects where a single task order will be issued based on selection criteria established at the ordering level, unless an exemption exists in accordance with FAR 16.507-6. The General Contractor (GC) shall serve as the single point of responsibility and must supervise, administer, coordinate, perform, and contract all management, labor, materials, equipment, and construction activities required to successfully execute each assigned project. Construction services will be required to be performed at federally owned and leased locations. The operational scope encompasses comprehensive general construction, repair, alteration, and modernization services for existing real property facilities. The General Contractor (GC) shall supervise, administer, perform, and contract all construction activities required to complete a project. Construction services include, but are not limited to office construction and/or renovations/repairs, office space renovations, MEP (Mechanical/Electrical/Plumbing) repairs/modifications/replacement, fire sprinkler systems repairs/modification/replacement, sitework, exterior construction repair and alterations (including facades and roofs), demolition (including abatement of hazardous materials), elevator modernizations, work in technically sensitive environments like laboratories, SCIF�s etc., work in high-security data centers and critical infrastructure control systems, construction work in high security buildings, as well as any other general construction activities. The scope will include design-build services. The GC may be required to utilize the following delivery methods to deliver projects for the GSA: 1. Design/Bid/Build (DBB) Traditional 2. Design/Build (D/B) The primary geography will cover: -All of Washington, D.C. -Virginia: Arlington County, Fairfax County, Loudon County, Independent Cities of Alexandria, Fairfax, and Falls Church -Maryland: Montgomery County, Prince George's County The Government may unilaterally expand the geography to cover any additional counties in the states of Maryland and Virginia. GSA reserves the right to expand, within scope, the geographic areas covered by the awarded contracts by bilateral agreement with any or all contract holders based on agency needs and requirements. The Maximum Ordering Limit (MOL) for this contract vehicle is $500,000,000.00. Meaning the cumulative total for all task orders awarded to all contractors over the life of the contract (5 Years) is not anticipated to exceed $500,000,000.00. There is no MOL per contractor or per performance period. The general task order range will be between $350,000.00 and $10,000,000.00. There will be a base period of one (1) year, and there will be four (4) option periods of one-year each, for a total possible performance period of five (5) years. The government intends to award approximately eighteen (18) contracts, inclusive of a target of twelve (12) contract reserves. However, the Government reserves the right to make more, fewer, or no awards, depending on the results of the evaluation, availability of funding, and the Government�s needs. The government is reserving three (3) contracts each for the following socioeconomic designations: 8(a), HUBZone, WOSB, SDVOSB, for a target of twelve (12) contract reserves. However, the Government reserves the right to make more, fewer, or no reserve awards, depending on the results of the evaluation, availability of funding, and the Government�s needs. Award Methodology This solicitation will be executed pursuant to Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 15.103-3 (RFO-2025-15), Highest technically rated with a fair and reasonable price approach. Pursuant to FAR Clause 52.215-1 Instructions to Offerors-Competitive Acquisition, and FAR 15.203 (RFO-2025-15), the Government intends to evaluate proposals and make competitive awards without negotiations with offerors although it reserves the right to negotiate should it be determined to be necessary. Competitive proposals shall be evaluated and assessed based on the factors specified in this solicitation. For this solicitation, all evaluation factors other than cost or price, when combined, are significantly more important than price. The Technical Evaluation Factors will be: Prior Experience Past Performance Evidence of Bonding Capacity: Go/No Go. (Minimum- $10M per project) Prior Experience is relatively more important than Past Performance. More detailed information regarding the technical factors and award methodology is included in the solicitation. Awards are anticipated to be made in February of 2027. Pre-Proposal Conference: A virtual pre-proposal conference will be held on Tuesday, October 6, 2026 @ 10:00AM EST and will be held via Google Meet. Registration is required by Monday, October 5, 2026 at 3:00PM EST. A link to the meeting will be provided upon registration. The Contracting Officer will also email the link to the email address provided by registrants. Do not share this link with others. A shared link may not allow entry to the virtual meeting. More information about the format and content of the pre-proposal conference is listed on page five (5) of the solicitation document. title: Commercial Solution Opportunity - Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) CONUS
description: This is a Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) issued under the authority of DFARS 212.70. The Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) is focused on modernizing business operations by actively seeking innovative commercial technologies, products and services that will enhance our ability to deliver the military pay benefit at a significant patron savings. Authorized under DFARS Subpart 212-70, this CSO enables DeCA to competitively procure solutions through a streamlined acquisition process, allowing for rapid decisions. This approach underscores our mission to expedite the award and delivery of critical technologies, products, and services, ensuring that DeCA can leverage advancements in the grocery resale industry swiftly and efficiently. By prioritizing speed in our contracting efforts, we aim to support the timely integration of cutting-edge technologies, products, and services that enhance our ability to: improve the commissary benefit; decrease costs without diminishing the benefit; improve processes that have a high risk of potential fraud, waste, or abuse; and reduce waste and decrease variation in processes. Contracts awarded under this authority will be structured as fixed-price contracts. Through this initiative, DeCA reaffirms its commitment to fostering innovation and enhancing business operations, ultimately delivering a vital benefit of the military compensation package that improves quality of life and readiness by providing grocery items at significant savings.

title: Market Intelligence: JDWC Progressive Design-Build OTA
description: (Please see attached Special Notice document W912HN27SA001 for full details and submission instructions). The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Savannah District, is issuing this Special Notice to conduct Market Intelligence for the Joint Deployment Warfighting Complex (JDWC) at Fort Bragg, North Carolina. This project will be procured utilizing a Progressive Design-Build (PDB) delivery method under the 10 U.S.C. 2808a Other Transaction (OT) authority for Construction. Project Snapshot: Design and construction of a high-security facility accommodating 750 personnel. Features include Secure Administrative Areas, Operations Centers, and SCIF spaces with stringent security requirements, along with fully redundant electrical/mechanical systems and major civil site modifications. Estimated Construction Budget: $350 Million. Acquisition Strategy: A streamlined, two-step Qualifications-Based Selection (QBS) process (Step 1: White Papers / Step 2: Pitch Meetings). Action Required: This is an Advance Notice for informational, planning, and market intelligence purposes only; it is not a formal Request for Proposal (RFP).Interested parties are requested to submit a capability statement (maximum of 5 pages) outlining their interest, bonding capacity, and relevant PDB and secure facility experience. Responses are due no later than October 29, 2026, at 4:00 PM Eastern Standard Time. All submissions must be electronic and emailed directly to the Points of Contact listed in the attached document. No hardcopy responses will be accepted.

title: Commercial Solution Opportunity - Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) CONUS
description: This is a Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) issued under the authority of DFARS 212.70. The Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) is focused on modernizing business operations by actively seeking innovative commercial technologies, products and services that will enhance our ability to deliver the military pay benefit at a significant patron savings. Authorized under DFARS Subpart 212-70, this CSO enables DeCA to competitively procure solutions through a streamlined acquisition process, allowing for rapid decisions. This approach underscores our mission to expedite the award and delivery of critical technologies, products, and services, ensuring that DeCA can leverage advancements in the grocery resale industry swiftly and efficiently. By prioritizing speed in our contracting efforts, we aim to support the timely integration of cutting-edge technologies, products, and services that enhance our ability to: improve the commissary benefit; decrease costs without diminishing the benefit; improve processes that have a high risk of potential fraud, waste, or abuse; and reduce waste and decrease variation in processes. Contracts awarded under this authority will be structured as fixed-price contracts. Through this initiative, DeCA reaffirms its commitment to fostering innovation and enhancing business operations, ultimately delivering a vital benefit of the military compensation package that improves quality of life and readiness by providing grocery items at significant savings.
